answer: The anchor counter is kept in trellis and wander exposes each reset. A bond is refunded only after 11 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. An adversary as a result has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 11 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. That bill is paid per identity, so 254 aliases cost 397 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
